topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: Answer these questions about famous American criminals.
question.text: This criminal was able to break out of what was said to be an "escape-proof" jail in 1934. He and his namesake gang terrorized the Midwest, allegedly robbing 24 banks and four police stations.
question.clue: Harold Cassidy and Wilhelm Loeser operated on this man and Homer Van Meter to change their appearance and fingerprints, which helped Jay Robert Nash claim that Jimmy Lawrence died after this man met with Polly Hamilton and Anna Sage.

swap.leadin: On "Black Sunday" during this period, so-called "black blizzards" swept through the plains states.
swap.text: "Okies" migrated west during what period of severe drought and agriculture damage in the 1930s?
swap.clue: This event saw numerous storms referred to as black blizzards.

question.leadin: In Schechter Poultry Corporation v. United States, known as the "sick chicken case," the Supreme Court unanimously decided that this law was unconstitutional.
question.text: Name this piece of legislation, signed in 1933, that established the National Recovery Administration, known for its Blue Eagle emblem, and the Public Works Administration, which survived the Supreme Court's ruling in Schechter.
question.clue: It set up an agency headed by General Hugh S. Johnson that, and it reduced maximum hours so that more people couple be employed, while its Section 7a was an important concession to labor unions.

swap.text: The Great Depression led to the election of Franklin Roosevelt, whose thrity nightly radio addresses from 1933 to 1934 were given this name due to their intimate and calming nature.
swap.clue: Similar speeches were given while their speaker was Governor of New York.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the U.S. Department of Labor.
question.text: This social worker and activist became the first woman to hold a cabinet position after her appointment as Secretary of Labor by FDR.
question.clue: Minimum wage and overtime was implemented by this secretary who enforced the Fair Labor Standards Act.

swap.text: The Second New Deal featured this bill, which established the rights of workers to form labor unions and engage in collective bargaining. It is alternatively known as the National Labor Relations Act of 1935.
swap.clue: Chief Justice Charles Hughes wrote the majority opinion in the resulting Supreme Court case against the Jones and Laughlin steel company that upheld the application of this law to interstate commerce.

question.leadin: Harcourt Morgan served on the board of directors for this agency, the constitutionality of which was upheld in the Ashwander case.
question.text: Name this agency created in 1933 that was intended to construct dams on a namesake body of water.
question.clue: It originated with a scheme to end dependance on Chilean nitrate imports during the First World War, and one of its chief opponents was John Lewis, who feared for the economic health of the coal mines.

swap.text: This informal bank policy, named after color-coded maps of classes of neighborhoods, excluded blacks and other racial minorities from taking out loans to buy homes in suburban areas.
swap.clue: Ending this practice was the main focus of the 1975 HDMA and the 1977 Community Reinvestment Act.

question.leadin: This man pushed for the popularization of radio as secretary of commerce, in which capacity he also vastly expand the department by siphoning off poorly managed duties from other agencies.
question.text: Name this man whose response to the Great Mississippi Flood helped propel him to the presidency, an engineer who saved millions of Europeans from starvation during World War I.
question.clue: As head of the Food Administration during World War I, this future President advocated for "Wheatless Wednesdays" and "Meatless Mondays."

swap.leadin: An entire floor of IBM machines in Baltimore's Candler Building was devoted to handling paperwork from this program.
swap.text: Name this program begun during the New Deal. Alan Greenspan headed a commission that increased contributions to this program's Trust Fund.
swap.answerHtml: Social Security [accept OAI or Old-Age Insurance Program; or Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance; or OASDI]
swap.clue: The Supreme Court case Flemming v. Nestor established that Congress can revise and amend this policy, which was expanded to include disability in 1954.

question.leadin: Note to Players: A description is acceptable for the first part. Handwriting analysis helped convict Bruno Hauptmann for the kidnapping of this person.
question.text: Name or describe this child whose 1932 kidnapping and murder led to a "Trial of the Century" and the passage of the Federal Kidnapping Act.
question.answerHtml: Charles Augustus Lindbergh Jr. [accept answers describing Charles Lindbergh’s son, accept the Lindbergh baby]

swap.leadin: Name the following about tariffs from American history.
swap.text: This 1930 tariff raised taxes on imports to the highest level in American history, prompting foreign countries to retaliate, helping spur on the Depression.
swap.clue: Franklin Delano Roosevelt signed the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934 as a direct Democratic response to this Republican legislation.

question.text: The "Black Cabinet" also pushed this organization to record over two thousand first-person accounts of former slaves. This Second New Deal organization employed hundreds of artists, musicians, and writers as part of Federal Project Number One.
question.answerHtml: Works Progress Administration [or WPA; or Work Projects Administration; accept Federal Writers’ Project]
question.clue: One branch of this organization was led by Hallie Flanagan, under whose leadership that branch undertook news reenactments called the "Living Newspaper," series, while another branch of this organization was responsible for producing the American Guide Series.

swap.text: This supervisor of the WPA was one of Roosevelt's closest advisors and served as Secretary of Commerce for Roosevelt near the end of his second term. He served as FDR's primary emissary to Britain during WWII and oversaw the lend lease program.
swap.clue: The phrase "Arsenal of Democracy" was suggested by this advisor to FDR, who crafted the WPA and was integral in implementing the Lend Lease Program.

question.leadin: This man got his start working at his brother James's tavern in the West Bottoms area.
question.text: Name this political boss who controlled Jackson County in the early 20th century. His downfall came after Lloyd Stark investigated him for income tax evasion.
question.clue: This political boss who built his machine from Kansas City, Missouri and brought people such as Guy Brasfield Park to power.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about photography in the first half of the 20th century.
swap.text: This photographer took pictures for the Farm Security Administration, documenting the Great Depression in Southern states, particularly Alabama. He collaborated with James Agee on Let Us Now Praise Famous Men.
swap.clue: A portrait of Allie May Burroughs was taken in by this photographer, who documented rural Alabama through staying with the Burroughs, Fields, and Tingle families. He compiled his photos into the collection Let Us Now Praise Famous Men.

question.text: As chair of Louisiana's Public Interest Commission, Long established a populist brand by suing a company in this industry for a rebate of its 20% rate hike. Elisha Gray was a pioneer in this industry.
question.answerHtml: telephone industry [or telegraph industry, or telecommunications industry; accept Cumberland Telephone and Telegraph Company]

swap.leadin: This man led a namesake board that advocated for the establishment of the Army Air Corps prior to the court martial of Billy Mitchell.
swap.text: Name this man who mediated the aggrelos, or agreement, that ended the Cristero War while serving as the U.S. ambassador to Mexico in the late 1920s.

question.leadin: Name these 20th-century pieces of antitrust legislation, FTP each.
question.text: The next major piece of antitrust legislation was this 1936 bill that explicitly defined the forms of price discrimination that the Clayton Act forbid.
question.clue: This law targeting secondary line competitive injury.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of conflict between print and radio news in America.
swap.text: Radio coverage of this event helped convince the newswire services to stop working with radio broadcasters. Liberty magazine published a series on John Condon's involvement in the aftermath of this event with the title "Jafsie Tells All."
swap.answerHtml: kidnapping of the Lindbergh baby [or kidnapping of Charles Augustus Lindbergh Jr.; accept murder or death in place of “kidnapping”; prompt on partial answer; prompt on Crime of the Century]
swap.clue: The suicidal Violet Sharpe was ruled out as a suspect in this case; many modern revisionist theories focus on the involvement of Isidor Fisch.
